elements.id-string-24: Text-to-image is a technique that converts natural language text into corresponding images, this technology covers some aspects of computer vision and natural language processing, and its application fields are very extensive, such as artistic creation, virtual scene generation, advertising design, game development, etc \cite{isola2017image} \cite{gatys2015neural} \cite{karras2017progressive} \cite{frolov2021adversarial} \cite{hald2020procedural}.
elements.id-string-25: \par Text-to-image is one of the most important applications of GAN (generative adversarial network) \cite{goodfellow2020generative}.
elements.id-string-26: In text-to-image synthesis, GAN’s generator receives text descriptions as input and generates images that match the descriptions.
elements.id-string-27: The discriminator is responsible for evaluating the authenticity of the generated image, and its goal is to distinguish the generated image from the real image.
elements.id-string-28: Generators and discriminators are trained through adversarial learning to gradually improve the quality of the generated images.
elements.id-string-29: The goal of GAN is to generate high-quality images of relevant content through semantics.
elements.id-string-30: This tasks presents two significant challenges: (1) Due to the instability of GAN structure, the generated images may become blurry and unrealistic.
elements.id-string-31: (2) Text information cannot be fully utilized by the generator, which limits the effectiveness of the text image fusion process and makes it difficult for the model to scale to higher resolution image synthesis.

elements.id-string-36: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) were introduced in a seminal paper by Ian Goodfellow and his colleagues in 2014 \cite{goodfellow2020generative}.
elements.id-string-37: Goodfellow and his colleagues introduced GAN as a new approach to generative modelling.
elements.id-string-38: They showed that GAN could generate realistic images and that the generated images were difficult to distinguish from real images.
elements.id-string-39: This was a major breakthrough in generative modelling, as previous methods were often limited in their ability to generate high-quality data.
elements.id-string-40: In 2017, a paper in ICCV presented a method for generating lifelike images using only a written description in natural language \cite{dong2017semantic}.
elements.id-string-41: They change the structure of GAN and find it performs better than the method proposed by Reed et al. \cite{reed2016generative}.
elements.id-string-42: Specifically, they trained a style encoder network to invert the generator network.
elements.id-string-43: While current methods can generate images with new attributes, they do not maintain the text-irrelevant details of the original image.
elements.id-string-44: In 2018 to address this issue, some authors at Yonsei University in NIPS 2018 introduced the Text-Adaptive Generative Adversarial Network (TAGAN), which generates semantically manipulated images while preserving the text-irrelevant details \cite{nam2018text}.
elements.id-string-45: This research paper proposes a solution to the problem of manipulating images based on natural language descriptions.
elements.id-string-46: The key idea of PPGN is to feed a random noise vector to the generative model and combine it with optimization techniques to guide the generative process \cite{nguyen2017plug}.
elements.id-string-47: LAPGAN is a generative model framework that combines Laplacian pyramid decomposition and GAN and aims to generate high-resolution images in a progressive manner \cite{denton2015deep}.
elements.id-string-48: The network takes a multi-scale approach and generates images in a coarse-to-fine fashion, with each level of the model generating a low-resolution version of the image.
elements.id-string-49: The goal of MirrorGAN is to achieve text-to-image conversion by learning fine-grained correspondences \cite{qiao2019mirrorgan}.
elements.id-string-50: The proposed method promotes consistency between text and image through backward information propagation during generation, and provides additional supervision signals through the discriminator in the reverse generation process.
elements.id-string-51: There have been several advancements in text-to-image generation using GAN.
elements.id-string-52: Here are some notable developments: Conditional GAN: In text-to-image synthesis, conditional GAN have been widely used where the generator takes a textual description as input and generates an image that matches the description \cite{mirza2014conditional}.
elements.id-string-53: Recent research has shown that conditioning the GAN on different factors such as object attributes, style, and layout can improve the quality and diversity of the generated images.
elements.id-string-54: The AttnGAN is a symbol of attention-based mechanisms \cite{xu2018attngan}.Attention-based mechanisms have been used to improve the quality and relevance of the generated images by focusing on the important parts of the text description.
elements.id-string-55: These mechanisms have been used to guide the generator to pay attention to the relevant words and phrases and use them to create the corresponding image.
elements.id-string-56: Multi-modal GANs have been developed to generate multiple images corresponding to a single text description, each depicting a different description aspect \cite{amirian2019social}.
elements.id-string-57: These models have been shown to generate diverse and high-quality images, capturing different interpretations of the same text description.
elements.id-string-58: VAE(Variational Autoencoder) is a type of generative model that has been explored for text-to-image synthesis \cite{kingma2013auto}.
elements.id-string-59: In VAE-based text-to-image synthesis, the model learns a latent space representation of the input text descriptions, which can be used to generate images.
elements.id-string-60: One of the primary advantages of using VAE-based models is their interpretability.
elements.id-string-61: But, there is still room for improvement to generate photo-realistic images that match the input textual description.
elements.id-string-62: PixelCNN was a generative model generates images pixel by pixel, where each pixel is conditioned on the previous pixels \cite{van2016conditional}.
elements.id-string-63: The key idea behind PixelCNN is to use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to model the distribution of the image pixels.
elements.id-string-64: PixelCNN has been shown to be effective at generating high-quality images, it has also been used for text-to-image synthesis, where the image is generated conditioned on an input text description.
elements.id-string-65: GAN-INT-CLS is the first application study that adds textual descriptions (i.e., sentence embedding vectors) as supervised signals to image generation \cite{reed2016generative}.
elements.id-string-66: The main goal of GAWWN is to estimate the scene layout of an image while generating it \cite{reed2016learning}.
elements.id-string-67: GAWWN improves the text-to-image performance by introducing Scene Layout Estimator in the image generation process \cite{zhang2017stackgan}.
elements.id-string-68: StackGAN (Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks) is used to gradually generate high-resolution images.

elements.id-string-120: \textbf{Datasets.} We chose two datasets, CUB bird \cite{WahCUB_200_2011} and COCO \cite{lin2014microsoft}, as our primary datasets referring to previous work.

elements.id-string-125: \textbf{Evaluation Details.} We choose the IS (Inception Score) and FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) to evaluate the quality of the generated images to evaluate our work.
elements.id-string-126: IS is evaluated by calculating the KL(Kullback–Leibler) divergence scatter of a conditional distribution and a marginal distribution, the higher the IS value then the higher the diversity entropy and the lower the quality entropy then the better the generative model \cite{salimans2016improved}.
elements.id-string-128: FID distance calculates the distance between the real sample, the generative sample in the feature space \cite{heusel2017gans}.
elements.id-string-129: The Inception network is first used to extract the features, then the feature space is modelled using a Gaussian model, and then the distance between the two features is solved for.
elements.id-string-130: A lower FID means higher quality and diversity of the images.

elements.id-string-194: Text-to-image technology, at the intersection of computer vision and natural language processing, converts textual descriptions into visual representations.
elements.id-string-195: It finds applications in art creation, virtual scene generation, advertising design, and game development etc.
elements.id-string-197: Within the field of image generation, an influential framework is the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN).
elements.id-string-198: By employing adversarial learning, wherein the generator and discriminator are trained simultaneously, the quality of the generated images progressively improves.
elements.id-string-199: GAN-based text-to-image models have rapidly evolved since the introduction of Text descriptions as supervised signals, demonstrated by GAN-INT-CLS~\cite{reed2016generative}.
elements.id-string-200: Notable advancements include the Adversarial What-Where Network (GAWWN) with its scene layout estimator~\cite{reed2016learning},  the Pixel Recurrent Neural Networks (PixelCNN) that model image pixel distributions using CNNs~\cite{van2016conditional}, and the Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (StackGAN and StackGAN-v2) that enhance image quality through multi-stage models or multiple generators and discriminators~\cite{zhang2017stackgan}\cite{zhang2018stackgan++}.
elements.id-string-201: Furthermore, the Semantics Disentangling GAN (SD-GAN) addresses latent space factor confusion with a self-distillation mechanism~\cite{yin2019semantics}.
elements.id-string-202: To improve the Text-to-image model performance, Attentional Generative Adversarial Network (AttnGAN) introduces the attention mechanism and the deep attention multimodal similarity model in the generation work, which enables AttnGAN to capture the word-level fine-grained information in the sentence.
elements.id-string-203: Thus allowing it to synthesise the advantages of fine-grained details of different subregions of an image by focusing on related words in the natural language description.
elements.id-string-204: However, the disadvantages of AttnGAN are also apparent.
elements.id-string-205: The AttnGAN contains multiple Attention models and multiple groups of baseline networks, which makes its model structure complex and has many parameters, which may lead to high computational complexity.

elements.id-string-258: \textbf{Datasets.} We selected two datasets: CUB Bird \cite{WahCUB_200_2011} and COCO \cite{lin2014microsoft}.
elements.id-string-259: The CUB dataset contains 11,788 bird images of 200 species, each with descriptions in 10 languages.
elements.id-string-260: Meanwhile, the COCO dataset has 80,000 images for training and 40,000 images for testing, each with descriptions in five languages.
elements.id-string-261: \textbf{Experiment settings.} Both our SEAttnGAN generator and discriminator use the Adam optimizer.
elements.id-string-262: The generator uses the parameters $\beta_{1} = 0$, $\beta_{2} = 0.9$ and the learning rate is $0.0001$ \cite{kingma2014adam}; while the discriminator uses the parameters $\beta_{1} = 0.0$, $\beta_{2} = 0.9$, the learning rate is $0.0004$.
elements.id-string-263: \textbf{Evaluation metrics.} Finally, we choose IS (Inception Score) and FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) to evaluate the quality of the generated image.
elements.id-string-264: IS measures \cite{salimans2016improved} the KL divergence between the generated image category distribution obtained by a pre-trained Inception V3 model and the real image category to represent the authenticity of the generated image.
elements.id-string-265: The smaller the KL divergence, the closer the category distribution of the generated image is to the real image.
elements.id-string-266: Higher IS values indicate better diversity and authenticity of generated images.
elements.id-string-267: It's not perfect though, as it may not capture the quality of detail and realism of the resulting image.
elements.id-string-268: Therefore, when evaluating image generation models, it is usually necessary to combine other indicators and human subjective evaluation for comprehensive consideration.
elements.id-string-269: Frechet Inception Distance (FID) \cite{heusel2017gans} is a metric used to measure the quality of image generation.
elements.id-string-270: It is based on the statistical feature difference between the generated image and the real image: it first uses a pre-trained image classifier (such as the Inception V3 model) to extract the feature representation of the real image and the generated image, and then uses the Fréchet distance to measure the difference between the two feature distributions.
elements.id-string-271: The difference between the sample mean and the covariance matrix of.
elements.id-string-272: The lower the value of FID, the better the quality of the generated image, and the higher the coincidence with the real image distribution.
elements.id-string-273: The advantage of FID over other metrics is that it can capture more subtle differences in image quality and has a high correlation with human subjective evaluation results.
elements.id-string-274: However, FID also has some limitations, such as requiring a pre-trained classifier and a large number of image samples.
